rules.note: Tell the chapter a line at a time, then open the choices.

actions.text:
OLD TAM THE FERRYMAN IS ILL.
TONIGHT YOU, PELL, TAKE THE FERRY.

THE FAR SHORE IS ACROSS FOGMERE.
THE LAMP HAS {oil} CUP OF OIL.

TWO WAIT ON THE DOCK: A LAMP SELLER
AND A SMALL, LOST FOX. WHO COMES?

SHE PAYS YOU IN OIL. THE LAMP
NOW HAS {oil} CUPS.

THE FOX CURLS UP ON A COIL
OF ROPE AND WATCHES THE WATER.

YOU PUSH OFF ALONE. THE DOCK
LIGHTS SHRINK BEHIND YOU.

actions.text:
HALFWAY OVER, THE FOG CLOSES IN.
YOU CANNOT SEE THE BOW.

A BELL RINGS, LOW AND SLOW,
SOMEWHERE OFF TO THE LEFT.
WHAT WILL YOU DO?

THE LAMP SHOWS THE BUOYS. {oil} CUPS
OF OIL LEFT. YOU STEER SAFELY ON.

NO OIL LEFT! YOU STEER BY THE
STARS YOU REMEMBER, HEART POUNDING.

YOU ROW HARD AT THE SOUND.
A BUOY SLIDES PAST, CLOSE!

THE FOX SNIFFS, THEN POINTS ITS NOSE.
YOU FOLLOW IT OUT OF THE FOG.

THERE IS NO FOX ABOARD. YOU WAIT,
AND DRIFT, AND WAIT SOME MORE.

actions.text:
THE FOG THINS BY REED ISLE.
SOMEONE IS WAVING FROM THE REEDS.

THE HERON KEEPER, STRANDED,
WET THROUGH AND SHIVERING.

THE NIGHT IS GETTING LATE.
WHAT DO YOU DO?

YOU WRAP THE KEEPER IN YOUR
COAT. THE HERON RIDES ON THE BOW.

YOU TOW THE KEEPER'S SKIFF
BEHIND YOU, STEADY AND SLOW.

YOU CALL THAT YOU WILL SEND
HELP, AND ROW ON INTO THE DARK.

actions.text: THE FAR SHORE COMES OUT OF THE NIGHT...

THE WHOLE TOWN WAITS WITH LANTERNS.
TAM WILL BE PROUD OF YOU.

SLOW, BUT EVERY SOUL IS SAFE.
THE PASSENGERS WAVE YOU HOME.

THE FASTEST CROSSING IN YEARS.
YOU WATCH THE SUN COME UP ALONE.

else.text:
YOU DRIFT UNTIL DAWN AND LAND
ON THE WRONG SHORE. TRY AGAIN?
